## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

- Local workspaces management with git metadata

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests

and no key action fires (Rule 111).

- Local workspaces management with git metadata

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**

- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks

**Parallel Execution:**

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests

only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from

(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

// cellWidth is the one width the table cuts and pads a cell by: the sum of
// ansi.FirstGraphemeCluster widths, which on plain text is ansi.StringWidth,
// the width Lip Gloss and the viewport use. Printable ASCII is measured by its
// length. An escape sequence is counted as text (Rule 122).
func cellWidth(s string) int

// fit is unchanged in signature and contract: plain text in, exactly `width`
// cells out (measured by ansi.StringWidth), no escape sequence of its own.
func fit(text string, width int, head bool) string

// fitASCII is fit for printable ASCII (0x20..0x7e only): byte slicing, no
// lipgloss call. It must return exactly what fitGraphemes returns for the same
// input (pinned by a test).
func fitASCII(text string, width int, head bool) string

// fitGraphemes is fit for anything else: truncateTail / truncateHead, then the
// existing lipgloss Width(w).MaxWidth(w).Inline(true) render, kept as is so tabs
// and newlines behave exactly as today. The cut is never wider than width, so
// MaxWidth (which uses ansi.Truncate) never has to act on it.
func fitGraphemes(text string, width int, head bool) string

// truncateTail keeps the start: whole grapheme clusters while they fit in
// width-1 cells, then truncationMarker. Text that fits is returned unchanged.
// Width 1 returns the marker alone. The result may be one cell short when a
// 2-cell cluster straddles the cut; fitGraphemes pads it.
func truncateTail(text string, width int) string

// truncateHead keeps the end (Column.TruncateHead): whole clusters taken from
// the right while they fit in width-1 cells, prefixed by the marker. When a
// 2-cell cluster straddles the cut it is dropped and a space pads after the
// marker ("… ト"), which is what runewidth.TruncateLeft produces today.
func truncateHead(text string, width int) string

// isPrintableASCII reports whether every byte of s is in 0x20..0x7e.
func isPrintableASCII(s string) bool

Both cuts walk `ansi.FirstGraphemeCluster(s, ansi.GraphemeWidth)` (returns the cluster and its
width), never `ansi.Truncate`/`TruncateLeft` (§1). Reference sketch for `truncateHead` (the
coder may avoid the slice; the tests decide):

```go
cs := clusters(text) // []struct{ s string; w int } via FirstGraphemeCluster
total := sum of w
if total <= width || width <= 0 { return text }
if width <= 1 { return truncationMarker }
keep, used, i := width-1, 0, len(cs)
for i > 0 && used+cs[i-1].w <= keep { i--; used += cs[i].w }
return truncationMarker + strings.Repeat(" ", keep-used) + join(cs[i:])
```

does today: `ESC` is a zero-width cluster and `[38;2;…m` counts one cell per byte. This is
deliberate and kept: it is the premise of Rule 122 ("a styled cell is over-measured and cut
mid-escape"), so `cellWidth` is defined as **the sum of the walk's cluster widths**, not as a
call to `ansi.StringWidth` (which skips escapes). On plain text the two are equal, and the
tests pin that equality; on styled text the table's measure over-counts, as before.

natural-width walk in `rebuild()` (already x/ansi through `lipgloss.Width`), `padToContent`,

2	# DEVDESK-280 — One width measure for VS16 emoji (datatable, Lip Gloss, viewport)
3	
4	Status: plan. Author: architect. Base: `main` at `5f76cc16`.
5	Inputs: story DEVDESK-280 (5 acceptance criteria), `docs/backlog.md` D114, D115 (item 2), D117,
6	`docs/architecture/ui-components.md`, `.claude/rules/tui-tables.md` (Rules 116, 122, 125).
7	
8	**Blocking questions: none.** Three choices were taken without asking; they are listed as
9	hypotheses in §8 (H1–H3) and can be reversed without touching the core of the change.
10	
11	## 1. What the code does today (measured, not assumed)
12	
13	`internal/ui/datatable/render.go`:
14	
15	| Site | Measure | Notes |
16	|---|---|---|
17	| `fit()` (every cell and every header title) | `runewidth.Truncate`, then `lipgloss…Width(w).MaxWidth(w).Inline(true).Render` | cut by runewidth, padded and re-cut by x/ansi |
18	| `truncateHead()` (`Column.TruncateHead`) | `runewidth.StringWidth/Truncate/TruncateLeft` | same, through `fit` |
19	| `rowLine` indicator cell | `runewidth.FillRight` | **deliberate**: follows `runewidth.DefaultCondition.EastAsianWidth` (ambiguous `● ○ ◐`), pinned by `TestRule116HoldsUnderEastAsianWidth` |
20	| `rebuild()` natural widths (`datatable.go:711,719`) | `lipgloss.Width` = x/ansi | already grapheme |
21	| `widths.go` sort arrow | `lipgloss.Width` | already grapheme |
22	
23	Probe of the current `fit` (scratch program, x/ansi v0.11.9, go-runewidth v0.0.31):
24	
25	| Input | Column | Today | ansi width | Defect |
26	|---|---|---|---|---|
27	| `✔️` | 1 | `""` | 0 | line one cell short, nothing says there was a value |
28	| `❤️❤️❤️❤️` | 3 | `"❤️"` | 2 | line one cell short (AC3) |
29	| `❤️❤️❤️❤️` | 5 | `"❤️❤️"` | 4 | one cell short, marker lost |
30	| `a❤️x` | 3 | `"a❤️"` | 3 | right width, but no `…`: the cut is silent |
31	| `x✔️` (head) | 2 | `"x"` | 1 | one cell short |
32	| `1️⃣2️⃣3️⃣` (keycaps) | 4 | whole string | 6 | **overflow** by two cells: neither runewidth (3) nor `MaxWidth` cuts it |
33	
34	Why: runewidth counts the cut as fitting (VS16 = 1), lipgloss `Width` pads nothing, then
35	`MaxWidth` (x/ansi) re-cuts *after* the padding, and a 2-cell cluster that does not fit
36	leaves a hole. When nothing is cut the width is already right (lipgloss pads by x/ansi):
37	that is why `TestSelectedRowWithEmojiMeasuresRenderedWidth` is green today.
38	
39	**x/ansi v0.11.9 is not self-consistent either**, which decides the design (§4):
40	`ansi.StringWidth("1️⃣2️⃣3️⃣") == 6` but `ansi.Truncate("1️⃣2️⃣3️⃣", 4, "…")` returns the whole
41	string (its ASCII branch counts the `1` as one cell and the keycap tail as zero), and
42	`lipgloss…MaxWidth` uses `ansi.Truncate`, so it cannot repair it. `ansi.TruncateLeft` keeps a
43	wide cluster that straddles the cut (`TruncateLeft("日本語テキスト", 11, "…")` → `"…スト"`,
44	5 cells for a budget of 4). Both functions are therefore unusable as the table's cut; the
45	primitive that *is* consistent with `ansi.StringWidth` is `ansi.FirstGraphemeCluster(s,
46	ansi.GraphemeWidth)`, which `StringWidth` itself sums.
47	
48	### 1.1 The other measuring sites (checked; out of scope, reasons given)
49	
50	- **Lip Gloss v2 and `bubbles/viewport` v2**: `ansi.StringWidth` (grapheme). They are the
51	  reference this story aligns on. Nothing to change.
52	- **The Bubble Tea v2 renderer** (`cursed_renderer.go`, ultraviolet `buffer.go:617`) measures
53	  with `ansi.WcWidth` (VS16 = 1) **by default**, and switches to `ansi.GraphemeWidth` only when
54	  the terminal answers mode 2027 (`tea.go:822`). This is not ours to change, and it does not
55	  depend on the datatable: Lip Gloss and the viewport border already pad by grapheme width, so
56	  on a terminal without 2027 a line holding a VS16 emoji can show its right border one cell
57	  off. That is the D117 manual check ("a VS16 emoji … no shift (mode 2027)"), unchanged by
58	  this story. After the change the datatable agrees with the frame around it in every case;
59	  before it, it disagreed with both.
60	- **`theme.StringWidth`, `TruncateWidth`, `TruncateTailWidth`, `gauge.go`, `path.go`,
61	  `components/footer_message.go`** (14 non-test call sites): runewidth on purpose. They follow
62	  East Asian ambiguous width (footer dot, `RowStatusLine`, pinned by
63	  `footer_activity_test.go`, `row_status_test.go` with `runewidth.DefaultCondition`). Switching
64	  them would break that and is not asked. They keep the VS16 divergence; it is re-pinned
65	  there (step 3), and a follow-up story is proposed (§9).
66	- **`theme.Truncate` (`box.go`)**: `lipgloss.Width` + `MaxWidth`, already x/ansi.
67	- **`internal/ui/viewer`** (`lines.go: wrapTokens`): wraps by **rune count**, not width. A
68	  CJK line or a VS16 emoji can already be mis-wrapped, and a wrap can split `❤` from its
69	  `U+FE0F`. A pre-existing, separate defect (it is not a width *measure*): follow-up story
70	  proposed (§9), not fixed here.
71	- **`spanRuns` / `splitCellRun`**: slice by rune index and are documented as single-width
72	  only (Rule 122). Their callers (gauges, Git Status, token bars) put no emoji in them.
73	  Unchanged.

78	|---|---|---|
79	| `REDACTED` | `datatable/width_test.go` | **replaced** (AC4), step 1 |

129	## 4. Design (option A)
130	
131	All in `internal/ui/datatable/render.go`. Signatures (unexported, package-internal):
132	
133	```go
134	// cellWidth is the one width the table cuts and pads a cell by: the sum of
135	// ansi.FirstGraphemeCluster widths, which on plain text is ansi.StringWidth,
136	// the width Lip Gloss and the viewport use. Printable ASCII is measured by its
137	// length. An escape sequence is counted as text (Rule 122).
138	func cellWidth(s string) int
139	
140	// fit is unchanged in signature and contract: plain text in, exactly `width`
141	// cells out (measured by ansi.StringWidth), no escape sequence of its own.
142	func fit(text string, width int, head bool) string
143	
144	// fitASCII is fit for printable ASCII (0x20..0x7e only): byte slicing, no
145	// lipgloss call. It must return exactly what fitGraphemes returns for the same
146	// input (pinned by a test).
147	func fitASCII(text string, width int, head bool) string
148	
149	// fitGraphemes is fit for anything else: truncateTail / truncateHead, then the
150	// existing lipgloss Width(w).MaxWidth(w).Inline(true) render, kept as is so tabs
151	// and newlines behave exactly as today. The cut is never wider than width, so
152	// MaxWidth (which uses ansi.Truncate) never has to act on it.
153	func fitGraphemes(text string, width int, head bool) string
154	
155	// truncateTail keeps the start: whole grapheme clusters while they fit in
156	// width-1 cells, then truncationMarker. Text that fits is returned unchanged.
157	// Width 1 returns the marker alone. The result may be one cell short when a
158	// 2-cell cluster straddles the cut; fitGraphemes pads it.
159	func truncateTail(text string, width int) string
160	
161	// truncateHead keeps the end (Column.TruncateHead): whole clusters taken from
162	// the right while they fit in width-1 cells, prefixed by the marker. When a
163	// 2-cell cluster straddles the cut it is dropped and a space pads after the
164	// marker ("… ト"), which is what runewidth.TruncateLeft produces today.
165	func truncateHead(text string, width int) string
166	
167	// isPrintableASCII reports whether every byte of s is in 0x20..0x7e.
168	func isPrintableASCII(s string) bool
169	```
170	
171	Both cuts walk `ansi.FirstGraphemeCluster(s, ansi.GraphemeWidth)` (returns the cluster and its
172	width), never `ansi.Truncate`/`TruncateLeft` (§1). Reference sketch for `truncateHead` (the
173	coder may avoid the slice; the tests decide):
174	
175	```go
176	cs := clusters(text) // []struct{ s string; w int } via FirstGraphemeCluster
177	total := sum of w
178	if total <= width || width <= 0 { return text }
179	if width <= 1 { return truncationMarker }
180	keep, used, i := width-1, 0, len(cs)
181	for i > 0 && used+cs[i-1].w <= keep { i--; used += cs[i].w }
182	return truncationMarker + strings.Repeat(" ", keep-used) + join(cs[i:])
183	```
184	
185	Prototyped in the scratch area: with this cut and the unchanged lipgloss render,
186	`ansi.StringWidth(fit(s, w, head)) == w` held for 20 017 strings (fixed VS16, keycap, ZWJ,
187	skin-tone, flag, CJK, combining, stray `U+FE0F`/`U+20E3`, Nerd Font cases plus 20 000 random
188	strings drawn from them) × widths 1..12 × both directions; outputs `fit("日本語テキスト", 4,
189	true) == "… ト"`, `fit("日本語テキスト", 5, true) == "…スト"`, `fit("1️⃣2️⃣3️⃣", 4, false) ==
190	"1️⃣… "`. The same corpus fails with `ansi.Truncate` (keycaps).
191	
192	An escape sequence inside a `Cell` (forbidden by Rule 122) is walked as text, as runewidth
193	does today: `ESC` is a zero-width cluster and `[38;2;…m` counts one cell per byte. This is
194	deliberate and kept: it is the premise of Rule 122 ("a styled cell is over-measured and cut
195	mid-escape"), so `cellWidth` is defined as **the sum of the walk's cluster widths**, not as a
196	call to `ansi.StringWidth` (which skips escapes). On plain text the two are equal, and the
197	tests pin that equality; on styled text the table's measure over-counts, as before.
198	
199	Unchanged on purpose: the indicator branch of `rowLine` (`runewidth.FillRight`), the
200	natural-width walk in `rebuild()` (already x/ansi through `lipgloss.Width`), `padToContent`,
201	`spanRuns`, `splitCellRun`.

# DEVDESK-280 — One width measure for VS16 emoji (datatable, Lip Gloss, viewport)

Status: plan. Author: architect. Base: `main` at `5f76cc16`.
Inputs: story DEVDESK-280 (5 acceptance criteria), `docs/backlog.md` D114, D115 (item 2), D117,
`docs/architecture/ui-components.md`, `.claude/rules/tui-tables.md` (Rules 116, 122, 125).

**Blocking questions: none.** Three choices were taken without asking; they are listed as
hypotheses in §8 (H1–H3) and can be reversed without touching the core of the change.

## 1. What the code does today (measured, not assumed)

`internal/ui/datatable/render.go`:

| Site | Measure | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `fit()` (every cell and every header title) | `runewidth.Truncate`, then `lipgloss…Width(w).MaxWidth(w).Inline(true).Render` | cut by runewidth, padded and re-cut by x/ansi |
| `truncateHead()` (`Column.TruncateHead`) | `runewidth.StringWidth/Truncate/TruncateLeft` | same, through `fit` |
| `rowLine` indicator cell | `runewidth.FillRight` | **deliberate**: follows `runewidth.DefaultCondition.EastAsianWidth` (ambiguous `● ○ ◐`), pinned by `TestRule116HoldsUnderEastAsianWidth` |
| `rebuild()` natural widths (`datatable.go:711,719`) | `lipgloss.Width` = x/ansi | already grapheme |
| `widths.go` sort arrow | `lipgloss.Width` | already grapheme |

Probe of the current `fit` (scratch program, x/ansi v0.11.9, go-runewidth v0.0.31):

| Input | Column | Today | ansi width | Defect |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `✔️` | 1 | `""` | 0 | line one cell short, nothing says there was a value |
| `❤️❤️❤️❤️` | 3 | `"❤️"` | 2 | line one cell short (AC3) |
| `❤️❤️❤️❤️` | 5 | `"❤️❤️"` | 4 | one cell short, marker lost |
| `a❤️x` | 3 | `"a❤️"` | 3 | right width, but no `…`: the cut is silent |
| `x✔️` (head) | 2 | `"x"` | 1 | one cell short |
| `1️⃣2️⃣3️⃣` (keycaps) | 4 | whole string | 6 | **overflow** by two cells: neither runewidth (3) nor `MaxWidth` cuts it |

Why: runewidth counts the cut as fitting (VS16 = 1), lipgloss `Width` pads nothing, then
`MaxWidth` (x/ansi) re-cuts *after* the padding, and a 2-cell cluster that does not fit
leaves a hole. When nothing is cut the width is already right (lipgloss pads by x/ansi):
that is why `TestSelectedRowWithEmojiMeasuresRenderedWidth` is green today.

**x/ansi v0.11.9 is not self-consistent either**, which decides the design (§4):
`ansi.StringWidth("1️⃣2️⃣3️⃣") == 6` but `ansi.Truncate("1️⃣2️⃣3️⃣", 4, "…")` returns the whole
string (its ASCII branch counts the `1` as one cell and the keycap tail as zero), and
`lipgloss…MaxWidth` uses `ansi.Truncate`, so it cannot repair it. `ansi.TruncateLeft` keeps a
wide cluster that straddles the cut (`TruncateLeft("日本語テキスト", 11, "…")` → `"…スト"`,
5 cells for a budget of 4). Both functions are therefore unusable as the table's cut; the
primitive that *is* consistent with `ansi.StringWidth` is `ansi.FirstGraphemeCluster(s,
ansi.GraphemeWidth)`, which `StringWidth` itself sums.

### 1.1 The other measuring sites (checked; out of scope, reasons given)

- **Lip Gloss v2 and `bubbles/viewport` v2**: `ansi.StringWidth` (grapheme). They are the
  reference this story aligns on. Nothing to change.
- **The Bubble Tea v2 renderer** (`cursed_renderer.go`, ultraviolet `buffer.go:617`) measures
  with `ansi.WcWidth` (VS16 = 1) **by default**, and switches to `ansi.GraphemeWidth` only when
  the terminal answers mode 2027 (`tea.go:822`). This is not ours to change, and it does not
  depend on the datatable: Lip Gloss and the viewport border already pad by grapheme width, so
  on a terminal without 2027 a line holding a VS16 emoji can show its right border one cell
  off. That is the D117 manual check ("a VS16 emoji … no shift (mode 2027)"), unchanged by
  this story. After the change the datatable agrees with the frame around it in every case;
  before it, it disagreed with both.
- **`theme.StringWidth`, `TruncateWidth`, `TruncateTailWidth`, `gauge.go`, `path.go`,
  `components/footer_message.go`** (14 non-test call sites): runewidth on purpose. They follow
  East Asian ambiguous width (footer dot, `RowStatusLine`, pinned by
  `footer_activity_test.go`, `row_status_test.go` with `runewidth.DefaultCondition`). Switching
  them would break that and is not asked. They keep the VS16 divergence; it is re-pinned
  there (step 3), and a follow-up story is proposed (§9).
- **`theme.Truncate` (`box.go`)**: `lipgloss.Width` + `MaxWidth`, already x/ansi.
- **`internal/ui/viewer`** (`lines.go: wrapTokens`): wraps by **rune count**, not width. A
  CJK line or a VS16 emoji can already be mis-wrapped, and a wrap can split `❤` from its
  `U+FE0F`. A pre-existing, separate defect (it is not a width *measure*): follow-up story
  proposed (§9), not fixed here.
- **`spanRuns` / `splitCellRun`**: slice by rune index and are documented as single-width
  only (Rule 122). Their callers (gauges, Git Status, token bars) put no emoji in them.
  Unchanged.

### 1.2 Tests that pin go-runewidth today

| Test | File | Effect of the change |
|---|---|---|
| `REDACTED` | `datatable/width_test.go` | **replaced** (AC4), step 1 |
| `TestDatatableWidthAgreesWithTheGraphemeWidth` | `datatable/width_test.go` | its subject becomes the theme helpers; moved, step 3 |
| `TestTheTableFillsTheViewportAtThreeWidths` | `datatable/width_test.go` | runewidth line check removed, VS16 names added, step 1 |
| `TestRunewidthMisreadsStyledTextWhichIsWhyCellIsPlain` | `datatable/render_test.go` | its premise ("the table measures with runewidth") stops being true; rewritten, step 3 |
| `TestRule116HoldsUnderEastAsianWidth` | `datatable/indicator_eastasian_test.go` | unchanged, stays green (indicator path keeps `FillRight`; text cells are ASCII) |
| `TestSelectedRowWithEmojiMeasuresRenderedWidth` | `datatable/indicator_pad_test.go` | unchanged, stays green |
| `TestRule116HoldsWithTheActivityColumnAtEveryWidth` | `agentusageview/activity_columns_test.go` | unchanged (asserts `RenderedWidth`, column widths) |
| `TestAGlyphIsOneRuneOfPlainText` | `indicator/indicator_test.go` | unchanged; it is what guarantees no indicator glyph can be a VS16 sequence |
| `gauge_test.go`, `path_test.go`, `row_status_test.go`, `footer_activity_test.go` | theme, components | unchanged (theme helpers untouched) |

### 1.3 Regression scan of every glyph the app ships

All 697 distinct non-ASCII string literals in non-test `internal/**/*.go` (Nerd Font icons,
`fileicon`, indicator glyphs, box drawing, arrows, `…`) were measured with both libraries:
**one** divergence, an escape string inside a comment (`render.go:23`). No icon, Nerd Font
glyph or indicator changes width with this change. What changes is user data in a cell
(file, container, branch, agent names, messages) that holds a VS16 sequence.

## 2. Non-functional requirements

- **Correctness (Rule 116):** every rendered table line spans exactly `RenderedWidth()`
  cells measured by `ansi.StringWidth`, VS16 included; a cut never splits a grapheme cluster
  and always shows `…`.
- **East Asian:** no change for the indicator cells (runewidth, by design) nor for the theme
  helpers. x/ansi honours `RUNEWIDTH_EASTASIAN=1` (read at init, `method.go`); a CJK *locale*
  without that variable is honoured by runewidth only. Text cells holding ambiguous-width
  glyphs under a locale-only East Asian terminal were already inconsistent (cut by runewidth,
  padded by x/ansi); after the change they follow x/ansi only. No test covers them today;
  declared, not fixed (§8, R2).
- **`View()` cost (DEVDESK-281 is separate; do not degrade):** measured on a scratch
  benchmark, 8 typical cells at width 20: today 11.1 µs, swap to `ansi.Truncate` alone
  13.4 µs (**+20 %**), swap + printable-ASCII fast path 2.1 µs (**−80 %**). On a 40-row,
  6-column table the plain swap would add about 70 µs per frame (about 8 % of the D114
  868 µs). The fast path is therefore part of this story (step 2), and the step's criterion is
  "`BenchmarkView` no worse than the baseline of step 0". It is not the DEVDESK-281
  optimisation: it only keeps this story from paying for its own change.
- **Exploitability:** no config, no new dependency (`x/ansi` is already a direct dependency;
  `go-runewidth` stays, for the indicator and the theme).

## 3. Options

| | Option | For | Against | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | **The datatable measures and cuts by walking `ansi.FirstGraphemeCluster`** (the primitive `ansi.StringWidth` sums, so plain-text widths equal Lip Gloss's), keeping `runewidth.FillRight` for the indicator cell only, plus a printable-ASCII fast path | One measure with Lip Gloss and the viewport, by construction; the library update that changes VS16 in Lip Gloss changes the table too; fixes the keycap overflow; small diff (one file) | A grapheme walk is slower than `runewidth.Truncate` (+20 % on `fit` measured with `ansi.Truncate`, same order expected) → needs the fast path; about 40 lines of cut code of our own instead of a library call | **Recommended** |
| A′ | As A, but cut with `ansi.Truncate` / `ansi.TruncateLeft` | Fewer lines | `ansi.Truncate` overflows on keycaps, `TruncateLeft` on straddling wide clusters (§1): the cut would not agree with the measure, which is the story's defect again | Rejected (prototyped: fails a 20 000-string random corpus that A passes) |
| B | Keep runewidth, then "bound the truncation": after the cut, re-measure with x/ansi and shrink until it fits, pad by x/ansi | No change of library in the hot path | Two measures stay, the very thing the story removes; a loop on every cut cell; still runewidth's view of what "fits" decides the marker position | Rejected |
| C | A local width function: runewidth + "VS16 after a text-presentation base counts 2" | Fast | Re-implements part of UAX #29 / UTS #51 in the app; diverges again on the next case x/ansi handles (keycaps `1️⃣`, text-default emoji + FE0E, skin tones…) | Rejected |
| D | A + switch `theme.*` width helpers to x/ansi too | One measure in the whole app | Breaks the East Asian handling the footer relies on (two test files pin it), out of the story's scope (datatable, Lip Gloss, viewport) | Rejected here, follow-up proposed (§9) |
| E | Follow the renderer: measure with `WcWidth` until mode 2027 is reported, then grapheme | Matches the terminal exactly | Lip Gloss and the viewport frame always measure grapheme, so the table would then disagree with its own border; needs the `ModeReportMsg` plumbed to every table | Rejected |

## 4. Design (option A)

All in `internal/ui/datatable/render.go`. Signatures (unexported, package-internal):

```go
// cellWidth is the one width the table cuts and pads a cell by: the sum of
// ansi.FirstGraphemeCluster widths, which on plain text is ansi.StringWidth,
// the width Lip Gloss and the viewport use. Printable ASCII is measured by its
// length. An escape sequence is counted as text (Rule 122).
func cellWidth(s string) int

// fit is unchanged in signature and contract: plain text in, exactly `width`
// cells out (measured by ansi.StringWidth), no escape sequence of its own.
func fit(text string, width int, head bool) string

// fitASCII is fit for printable ASCII (0x20..0x7e only): byte slicing, no
// lipgloss call. It must return exactly what fitGraphemes returns for the same
// input (pinned by a test).
func fitASCII(text string, width int, head bool) string

// fitGraphemes is fit for anything else: truncateTail / truncateHead, then the
// existing lipgloss Width(w).MaxWidth(w).Inline(true) render, kept as is so tabs
// and newlines behave exactly as today. The cut is never wider than width, so
// MaxWidth (which uses ansi.Truncate) never has to act on it.
func fitGraphemes(text string, width int, head bool) string

// truncateTail keeps the start: whole grapheme clusters while they fit in
// width-1 cells, then truncationMarker. Text that fits is returned unchanged.
// Width 1 returns the marker alone. The result may be one cell short when a
// 2-cell cluster straddles the cut; fitGraphemes pads it.
func truncateTail(text string, width int) string

// truncateHead keeps the end (Column.TruncateHead): whole clusters taken from
// the right while they fit in width-1 cells, prefixed by the marker. When a
// 2-cell cluster straddles the cut it is dropped and a space pads after the
// marker ("… ト"), which is what runewidth.TruncateLeft produces today.
func truncateHead(text string, width int) string

// isPrintableASCII reports whether every byte of s is in 0x20..0x7e.
func isPrintableASCII(s string) bool
```

Both cuts walk `ansi.FirstGraphemeCluster(s, ansi.GraphemeWidth)` (returns the cluster and its
width), never `ansi.Truncate`/`TruncateLeft` (§1). Reference sketch for `truncateHead` (the
coder may avoid the slice; the tests decide):

```go
cs := clusters(text) // []struct{ s string; w int } via FirstGraphemeCluster
total := sum of w
if total <= width || width <= 0 { return text }
if width <= 1 { return truncationMarker }
keep, used, i := width-1, 0, len(cs)
for i > 0 && used+cs[i-1].w <= keep { i--; used += cs[i].w }
return truncationMarker + strings.Repeat(" ", keep-used) + join(cs[i:])
```

Prototyped in the scratch area: with this cut and the unchanged lipgloss render,
`ansi.StringWidth(fit(s, w, head)) == w` held for 20 017 strings (fixed VS16, keycap, ZWJ,
skin-tone, flag, CJK, combining, stray `U+FE0F`/`U+20E3`, Nerd Font cases plus 20 000 random
strings drawn from them) × widths 1..12 × both directions; outputs `fit("日本語テキスト", 4,
true) == "… ト"`, `fit("日本語テキスト", 5, true) == "…スト"`, `fit("1️⃣2️⃣3️⃣", 4, false) ==
"1️⃣… "`. The same corpus fails with `ansi.Truncate` (keycaps).

An escape sequence inside a `Cell` (forbidden by Rule 122) is walked as text, as runewidth
does today: `ESC` is a zero-width cluster and `[38;2;…m` counts one cell per byte. This is
deliberate and kept: it is the premise of Rule 122 ("a styled cell is over-measured and cut
mid-escape"), so `cellWidth` is defined as **the sum of the walk's cluster widths**, not as a
call to `ansi.StringWidth` (which skips escapes). On plain text the two are equal, and the
tests pin that equality; on styled text the table's measure over-counts, as before.

Unchanged on purpose: the indicator branch of `rowLine` (`runewidth.FillRight`), the
natural-width walk in `rebuild()` (already x/ansi through `lipgloss.Width`), `padToContent`,
`spanRuns`, `splitCellRun`.

## 5. Implementation plan

Commands used throughout:

```bash
T=./internal/ui/datatable
go test $T -count=1                       # the package
go test $T -count=2                       # HOME / global-state hygiene
go test ./internal/ui/... -count=1        # every table view
mise run lint
```

### Step 0 — baseline benchmark (XS, independent, first)

- **File:** `internal/ui/datatable/bench_test.go` (new).
- **Write:** `BenchmarkFit(b *testing.B)` — sub-benchmarks `ascii`, `ascii-cut`,
  `cjk`, `vs16`, each calling `fit` over a fixed corpus at widths 8 and 20.
  `BenchmarkView(b *testing.B)` — a 120-wide, 40-row table, 6 columns (`indicatorConfig`
  plus text columns) of realistic ASCII cells (image refs, states, ports, dates), one
  `m.View()` per iteration, cursor on row 3.
- **Run on the current code and record** in the PR description:
  `go test $T -run '^$' -bench 'BenchmarkFit|BenchmarkView' -benchmem -count=7`.
- **Done when:** the numbers of `main` are recorded. No production change.

### Step 1 — the datatable measures with x/ansi (S; after step 0)

Tests first (red on `main`), in `internal/ui/datatable/width_test.go` unless stated:

1. **`TestDatatableMeasuresVS16LikeAnsi`** (replaces `REDACTED`;

2. **`TestAVS16CutNeverSplitsACluster`** (AC3, unit level). For the same strings, widths 1..10,
   both directions: strip the trailing padding and the marker, the rest is a prefix (tail cut)
   or a suffix (head cut) of the input that ends/starts **on a grapheme-cluster boundary of
   the input**; and when the input does not fit, the output contains `…`. Helper
   `clusterBounds(s string) map[int]bool` built with `ansi.FirstGraphemeCluster(s[i:],
   ansi.GraphemeWidth)`. Red today: `fit("a❤️x", 3, false)` has no marker.
3. **`REDACTED`** (AC3, table level). A table with a
   `SizingFixed` `Name` column of `MinWidth` 3 and 5 (`indicatorConfig`-style `Config[row]`),

   Red today (`❤️❤️❤️❤️` in 3 cells renders 2).
4. **`TestTheTableFillsTheViewportAtThreeWidths`** (edit). Add `"a❤️x"` and `"✔️ ok"` to

5. **`TestTruncateHeadKeepsWideClustersWhole`** (in `measure_test.go`). CJK regression for the

6. **`FuzzFitSpansTheColumn`** (new, `width_test.go`). Seeds: every string of `agreedWidths`

   UTF-8 and any input with a control character (`unicode.IsControl`: tabs and newlines go
   through lipgloss and are out of scope); for `w` in 1..40 and both directions,
   `ansi.StringWidth(fit(s, w, head)) == w`. Seeds run under `mise run test`; exploration is

Then the code, `internal/ui/datatable/render.go`:

- Add `cellWidth` (cluster-walk sum, §4), `truncateTail`, and rewrite `truncateHead`, both
  walking `ansi.FirstGraphemeCluster` (§4; **not** `ansi.Truncate`/`TruncateLeft`). Rewrite
  `fit` with `fitGraphemes` semantics for now (step 2 adds the fast path): the cut, then the
  same lipgloss render as today. Compute only the cut that is used (today the tail cut is
  computed even when `head`).
- Drop the `runewidth` import except for `runewidth.FillRight` in `rowLine` (indicator), whose

142	func fit(text string, width int, head bool) string

145	// lipgloss call. It must return exactly what fitGraphemes returns for the same

147	func fitASCII(text string, width int, head bool) string

151	// and newlines behave exactly as today. The cut is never wider than width, so
152	// MaxWidth (which uses ansi.Truncate) never has to act on it.
153	func fitGraphemes(text string, width int, head bool) string

155	// truncateTail keeps the start: whole grapheme clusters while they fit in
156	// width-1 cells, then truncationMarker. Text that fits is returned unchanged.
157	// Width 1 returns the marker alone. The result may be one cell short when a
158	// 2-cell cluster straddles the cut; fitGraphemes pads it.
159	func truncateTail(text string, width int) string

161	// truncateHead keeps the end (Column.TruncateHead): whole clusters taken from
162	// the right while they fit in width-1 cells, prefixed by the marker. When a
163	// 2-cell cluster straddles the cut it is dropped and a space pads after the
164	// marker ("… ト"), which is what runewidth.TruncateLeft produces today.
165	func truncateHead(text string, width int) string

171	Both cuts walk `ansi.FirstGraphemeCluster(s, ansi.GraphemeWidth)` (returns the cluster and its
172	width), never `ansi.Truncate`/`TruncateLeft` (§1). Reference sketch for `truncateHead` (the
173	coder may avoid the slice; the tests decide):
174	
175	```go
176	cs := clusters(text) // []struct{ s string; w int } via FirstGraphemeCluster
177	total := sum of w
178	if total <= width || width <= 0 { return text }
179	if width <= 1 { return truncationMarker }
180	keep, used, i := width-1, 0, len(cs)
181	for i > 0 && used+cs[i-1].w <= keep { i--; used += cs[i].w }
182	return truncationMarker + strings.Repeat(" ", keep-used) + join(cs[i:])
183	```
184	
185	Prototyped in the scratch area: with this cut and the unchanged lipgloss render,
186	`ansi.StringWidth(fit(s, w, head)) == w` held for 20 017 strings (fixed VS16, keycap, ZWJ,
